claims.text: Replacing 5–10 at% Ti with Hf in NiTi raises the transformation temperature.
Hf substitution produces a clearer temperature-dependent switch in plastic-deformation mechanisms.
Plasticity in high-temperature austenite is primarily dislocation-mediated.
Plasticity in low-temperature martensite is dominated by martensitic transformation.
Substitutional Hf enhances lattice distortion in the NiTi matrix.
Hf substitution affects the stability of the austenite and martensite phases.
Hf substitution changes the interface structure between austenite and martensite.
The Hf-induced increase in transformation temperature and phase stability causes the proposed switch in deformation mechanism.
The proposed switch in deformation mechanism alters yield stress.
The proposed switch in deformation mechanism alters recoverable strain.
Below Ms, the Hf-modified alloy has a higher yield stress.
Below Ms, the Hf-modified alloy exhibits superelastic effects due to martensitic transformation.
Above Ms, deformation is dominated by conventional dislocation motion.
Above Ms, changes in mechanical behavior are less pronounced.
Standard Hf-free NiTi shows a more gradual and less distinct temperature-induced transition in deformation mechanisms than Hf-modified NiTi.
The proposed behavior applies at Hf substitution levels of approximately 5–10 at%.
The magnitudes of changes in yield stress, recoverable strain, and transformation temperature depend on processing conditions and exact Hf content.

contradictions.description: The low-temperature state is described as already martensitic, yet its plasticity and superelastic response are attributed to martensitic transformation without clarifying what remaining phase transforms or distinguishing transformation-induced strain from martensite reorientation.

The testing conditions require temperatures spanning above and below the full transformation range, whereas the stated boundary is limited to room temperature through only just above the martensitic transformation; the applicable temperature interval is therefore ambiguous.
